verses.text: These were David's sons born in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam from Jezreel. His second was Daniel, whose mother was Abigail from Carmel.
His third was Absalom, son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur. His fourth was Adonijah, son of Haggith.
His fifth was Shephatiah, son of Abital. His sixth was Ithream, son of his wife Eglah.
These six were born to David in Hebron, where he ruled for seven years and six months. He ruled for thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
In Jerusalem, Bathshua daughter of Ammiel bore him four sons: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon.
Nine other sons were born there: Ibhar, Elishama, and Eliphelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia,
and Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
These were David's sons, besides the sons of his concubines. Tamar was their sister.
Solomon's son was Rehoboam. The family line continued through Rehoboam's son Abijah, then Asa and Jehoshaphat,
then Joram, Ahaziah, and Joash,
then Amaziah, Azariah, and Jotham,
then Ahaz, Hezekiah, and Manasseh,
then Amon and Josiah.
Josiah's firstborn was Johanan, his second was Jehoiakim, his third was Zedekiah, and his fourth was Shallum.
Jehoiakim's sons were Jeconiah and Zedekiah.
The sons of Jeconiah, who was taken captive, included Shealtiel,
as well as Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
Pedaiah's sons were Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel's sons included Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith was their sister.
He also had five sons named Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab Hesed.
Hananiah's sons were Pelatiah and Jeshaiah. The family records also include the sons of Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah, and Shecaniah.
Shecaniah's son was Shemaiah. The record counts six sons of Shemaiah and names Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
Neariah had three sons: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.
Elioenai had seven sons: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.
